cards.title: A virtual twin for biosafety labs, built for biosafety officers and…
cards.one_line: A virtual twin for biosafety labs, built for biosafety officers and lab managers at university and biotech BSL-2/3 facilities. Today, risk assessments and containment reviews live in static PDFs and get revisited once a year. I want each lab to have a living digital twin: its floor plan, equipment, airflow and pressure zones, and SOPs, kept in a persistent workspace. Agents then run “what if” scenarios against it (a spill in the BSC, an HVAC failure, a door interlock fault, a new protocol or agent being introduced), check the outcome against the lab’s own biosafety manual and CDC/NIH guidance, and hand the officer an audit-ready report with the gaps flagged. HarnessRouter is the backend that makes this practical: one isolated, persistent sandbox per lab, so sensitive facility data never mixes, and one API that lets me route simulation and code-heavy work to on.

The goal is to help engineering teams build systems that can intelligently route queries across different LLMs, retrieval sources, and tools based on the task, complexity, latency, cost, and confidence requirements. cards.title: Our idea is to build an app that helps people find nearby events tied…
cards.one_line: Our idea is to build an app that helps people find nearby events tied to a specific interest. For example, students looking to break into startups or begin their internship search could use it to find hackathons, pitch competitions, and networking nights in their area. It works in both directions: venture capitalists can discover student events worth attending to scout emerging talent, and students can find events where they’re likely to meet investors and founders. Under the hood, the app works as a web scraper. It continuously pulls event listings from sources like Eventbrite, Meetup, Luma, Devpost, university calendars, and club pages, then organizes them into a single searchable feed. Users choose their interests and location, and the app filters and ranks events by relevance, date, and distance, so they spend less time digging through scattered websites and more time showing up to the events that matter to them.

cards.title: Tripwire: automatic regression detection and failover for AI agent…
cards.one_line: Tripwire: automatic regression detection and failover for AI agent harnesses. Coding agents like Claude Code and Codex ship new harness versions every few days, and some quietly make the agent worse even when the model is unchanged. Anthropic traced its own April 2026 Claude Code quality drop to three harness changes, not the model. Today, teams building on these agents only find out when users complain. Tripwire runs a team’s own task suite on HarnessRouter whenever a harness releases a new version. It compares pass rate, cost and latency against the last known good version. If the new release regresses, Tripwire alerts the team and reroutes their traffic to the previous version or a stronger harness, with an audit trail explaining why. Public trackers report whether an agent got worse on benchmarks; Tripwire protects your own product and fixes your routing automatically. It is for startups and product teams building on agent harnesses through HarnessRouter. It uses HarnessRouter’s sandboxes, traces, Harness Arena and routing. I will pilot it with early-stage teams during build week.

cards.title: I'm building Nabi (nabiai.tech), an AI front desk for small clinics…
cards.one_line: I'm building Nabi (nabiai.tech), an AI front desk for small clinics and salons: it answers calls and texts, books appointments, and runs the clinic's calendar, payments and client records. Real clinics in BC and the Bay Area use it today. Clinic staff send feedback from inside the app, like "the calendar should do X" or "this text sounds wrong". Today each request starts a GitHub Action, and a coding agent turns it into a pull request. I want to move that onto HarnessRouter so every request gets its own isolated container running Claude Code or Codex against our repo. The agent reproduces the issue, makes the fix, and runs our typecheck and tests. The clinic gets back a preview link to approve, all through one API and without being tied to one vendor's harness. It's for front-desk staff and owners at small clinics. They can't file tickets or wait weeks for a dev team, so they should be able to say what's broken in plain words and see it fixed the same day.
